extracted.intended_audience: Yale faculty, researchers, and staff preparing grant proposals (NIH/NSF/NEH/Mellon and other funders)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing competitive grant proposals across STEM and humanities at Yale, with funder-specific expectations (NIH, NSF, NEH, Mellon) and institutional advice about leveraging Yale resources and avoiding common pre-submission errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims: standard four-paragraph structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the standard four-paragraph layout for the Specific Aims page (NIH-relevant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the conventional structure (significance/problem, gap/hypothesis, aims, impact/approach). Keep concise; iterate 10+ times and consider including a conceptual figure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims: hypothesis-driven aims
rubrics_metrics.description: State hypothesis-driven aims rather than exploratory-sounding goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure aims are framed around testable hypotheses appropriate for the funding mechanism and reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims: aim independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Each specific aim should be independently valuable and executable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid aim interdependence that creates single-point failures; reviewers expect independent aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims: conceptual figure encouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a conceptual figure on the Specific Aims page where helpful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear, simple figure can communicate the study design or mechanism to non-specialist reviewers; use sparingly and iteratively refine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims: iterate many times
rubrics_metrics.description: Iterate the Specific Aims page 10+ times for polish and clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple revisions help sharpen hypothesis, aims, and reviewer-facing framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance: frame for non-specialist reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame significance so non-specialist reviewers understand the problem and stakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid jargon; explain why the question matters to the field and to the funder's mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance: cite high-impact recent papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate engagement with current high-impact literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite recent, relevant, high-impact work to show awareness of the field and current debates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance: connect to institute/funder mission
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly connect the project to the mission/priorities of the target funding institute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For NIH, link to the relevant institute's priorities; for foundations, show strategic alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation: novel application or concept
rubrics_metrics.description: Present innovation as a novel application or conceptual advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame innovation realistically — novel yet feasible; explain how it differs from prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach: structure each aim with subsections
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize the Approach by aim, using subsections for clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each aim should have clear methods, expected outcomes, and contingency plans; makes reviewer evaluation easier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach: statistical analysis plan with power
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a statistical analysis plan and power calculations where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete power/sample size justification tied to primary outcomes; link methods to hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach: sample size justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Justify sample sizes quantitatively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include assumptions, effect sizes, and calculations; reviewers expect transparent rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach: explicit rigor and reproducibility language
rubrics_metrics.description: Address rigor and reproducibility directly in the Approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss controls, blinding/randomization where relevant, data management, and reproducibility practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach: authentication of resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe authentication of key resources (reagents, cell lines, datasets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide plans to verify materials and methods to avoid irreproducible findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach: account for sex as a biological variable
rubrics_metrics.description: Address sex as a biological variable when relevant to the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify how sex/gender will be considered in design, analysis, and interpretation per funder expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach: discuss alternatives and contingencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe alternative strategies and contingency plans for key aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate foresight about potential obstacles and realistic backup plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator: productivity matched to career stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Align investigator productivity and role with their career stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For early-career investigators show potential and plan; for senior investigators show appropriate leadership and productivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment: cite Yale-specific resources
rubrics_metrics.description: List Yale facilities, centers, and institutional resources that support the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly reference relevant Yale cores (YCCI, Yale Cancer Center, Beinecke, etc.) to strengthen Environment and feasibility claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of support: be specific
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain letters of support that are specific about commitment and role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters should state what resources or contributions will be provided and be tailored to the proposal rather than generic.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEH: significance to humanities scholarship
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate the project's significance to humanities scholarship for NEH proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain contribution to historiography, interpretation, or disciplinary debates; situate within current scholarship.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEH: methodology specific to discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe methods appropriate and specific to the humanities discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outline research practices, archival methods, editorial approaches, or theoretical frameworks as relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEH: include project narrative, work plan, and budget
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH applications should include a project narrative, detailed work plan, and realistic budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connect tasks to timeline and deliverables; justify costs relative to proposed activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEH: letters from senior scholars
rubrics_metrics.description: Secure endorsement letters from senior scholars when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Senior scholar letters should attest to scholarly significance and the applicant's capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEH: final product specified
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the final scholarly product (book, edition, digital project) for humanities proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be concrete about intended outputs and how they will be disseminated or preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mellon: long-term, transformative focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Mellon-funded projects should aim for long-term, transformative scholarly impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate sustained change, institutional capacity-building, or transformative scholarship rather than short-term outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mellon: institutional/strategic alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Show strategic alignment with Mellon priorities; many Mellon awards emphasize institutional initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with institutional leaders and Office of Development for larger, strategic proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mellon: senior leader letters of support
rubrics_metrics.description: Include letters from senior institutional leaders for Mellon proposals when required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters should speak to institutional commitment, sustainability, and alignment with strategic goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF: intellectual merit and broader impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Address both Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts explicitly for NSF proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how the work advances knowledge (intellectual merit) and how it benefits society, education, or diversity (broader impacts).

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH: follow standard NIH conventions and institute framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to NIH norms (Specific Aims, Significance, Innovation, Approach) and tie the project to institute priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NIH‐style structure, cite relevant NIH resources (YCCI, NCI), and frame translational relevance where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Yale resources: explicitly leverage institutional assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage Yale archives, centers, and cores as strengths in applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite Beinecke Library, Yale Center for British Art, Yale Cancer Center, YCCI, and other relevant units to strengthen Environment and feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a realistic and well-justified budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSP looks for budgets aligned with scope; unrealistic or under/over-inflated budgets harm competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance: address regulatory and administrative requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proactively address compliance (IRB/IACUC, data sharing, conflicts of interest, export controls) in proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify approvals needed and timelines; missing compliance plans are commonly flagged pre-submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-submission checks: correct budget errors
rubrics_metrics.description: OSP will check and flag budget calculation or formatting errors before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review budgets carefully, ensure consistency across forms and justification sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-submission checks: close compliance gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: OSP will identify missing or incomplete compliance documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide required approvals or plans (human subjects, animal care, biosafety) ahead of deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-submission checks: resolve subaward complications
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure subaward scopes, budgets, and institutional approvals are in order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early coordination with subaward institutions prevents submission delays or budget rework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-submission checks: correct format violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix formatting and page-limit violations that can cause administrative rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to font, margin, and page-limit rules of the agency and Yale OSP submission guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-submission checks: include all required sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure no required sections are missing from the proposal package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-check agency checklist and Yale OSP requirements to avoid omitted sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humanities winning qualities: clear novel scholarly contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Humanities proposals must articulate a clear, novel contribution to scholarship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how the project pushes historiography, theory, or interpretation forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humanities winning qualities: engagement with relevant historiography
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage directly with the relevant historiography or disciplinary debates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate familiarity with key debates and position your work within them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humanities winning qualities: specific methodology and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a specific methodology and a clear timeline with deliverables for humanities projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie tasks to months/years and describe outcomes (chapters, editions, digital products).

rubrics_metrics.name: Humanities winning qualities: cohort or institutional alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Show how the project fits within a cohort, department, or institutional agenda when relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foundations often prefer projects aligned with institutional strengths and sustainable engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Yale academic voice: disciplinary excellence and engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate disciplinary excellence, engagement with current debates, and long-term scholarly contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Yale emphasizes high standards; articulate lasting scholarly impact and contribution to the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinarity: be genuine and substantive
rubrics_metrics.description: Interdisciplinary proposals should demonstrate genuine, substantive integration across fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite concrete cross-school collaborations, joint resources, and how disciplinary methods are integrated rather than superficially combined.
